summary: Implementation plan for multi-orchestrator streaming ingestion, fingerprint detection benchmarks, corrupted line resilience, and subagent tree linking in lumen-session. Amended 2026-08-20: CodexAdapter and OpenCodeAdapter criteria were rewritten against real, directly-verified wire formats (real Codex CLI rollout event_msg/item_completed/token_count envelope; real OpenCode SQLite session/message/part/event tables), replacing entirely fictional prior formats. ClaudeCodeAdapter/AgyAdapter criteria were tightened against real field names. New criteria added for Codex service_tier, ClaudeCode explicit-null rejection, otel_conversation_id precedence, AGY's real transcript path, and Qwen fingerprint detection.

tasks.title: CanonicalTranscript Model Extensions: ParseFailureRecord, otel_conversation_id, service_tier, reasoning_output_tokens
tasks.reasoning: Foundational plumbing task inserted ahead of every adapter task in this amendment pass. CRIT-LUMEN-025 requires a parse-failure record that SURVIVES parse_stream (CanonicalTranscript.parse_failures), CRIT-LUMEN-162 requires a place to record Codex's service_tier, CRIT-LUMEN-164 requires the redesigned singular CanonicalTranscript.otel_conversation_id (SPEC-LUMEN-005-ANALYSIS's api_surface, replacing otel_request_ids: SmallVec<[CompactString; 2]>), and CRIT-LUMEN-110 requires reasoning_output_tokens kept distinct from output_tokens on TokenEconomics. All four are added here, in one place, before any adapter task depends on them, so every downstream adapter task in this plan sees the fields already present rather than each task racing to add them inconsistently. subagent_role is NOT added here -- it is already declared in SPEC-LUMEN-001-MODEL's api_surface and is PLAN-LUMEN-001-MODEL's responsibility; this task only assumes it exists on CanonicalTranscript by the time TASK-SESSION-008 runs.

tasks.title: AGY Adapter Thinking Blocks, Double-Encoded Tool Args & Real Transcript Path Resolution
tasks.reasoning: CRIT-LUMEN-021's field/value vocabulary (step_index/source=USER_EXPLICIT|MODEL) was already correctly implemented and tested; left unchanged. CRIT-LUMEN-027 was extended this pass to require tool_calls[] extraction (previously undocumented) with a specific, confirmed-real gotcha: each tool_call arg value is itself a JSON-encoded string requiring a second parse pass, with a fallback to the raw string on inner-parse failure. CRIT-LUMEN-165 (new-to-this-task, though not a newly-added criterion ID) requires AgyAdapter to resolve the real transcript path directly, bypassing the ~/.gemini/logs symlink layer; since parse_stream only receives a reader (not a path), this is implemented as a new pure path-construction associated function, independently testable without filesystem I/O. tasks.title: CodexAdapter Real event_msg Envelope: Fingerprint, Turn Mapping, Cumulative Token Accounting & Service Tier
tasks.reasoning: Full rewrite. The prior CRIT-LUMEN-106/109/110 fingerprinted and parsed a raw OpenAI Chat Completions API shape (choices[]/prompt_tokens/thread_id at the envelope's top level) that was confirmed this session, against a real local ~/.codex/sessions/.../rollout-*.jsonl file and cross-validated by ccusage's real Rust Codex adapter, to not exist in real Codex CLI output. Real rollout lines use {timestamp, ordinal, type, payload} with type=event_msg and payload.type in {item_completed, token_count, thread_settings_applied, ...}; thread_id lives on payload, not the envelope top level; token_count carries a cumulative total_token_usage (last-write, not summed, unlike OpenCodeAdapter's per-line deltas); CRIT-LUMEN-162 (new) requires capturing thread_settings_applied's service_tier. All prior test/fixture content referencing choices/prompt_tokens/completion_tokens is deleted, not amended in place, since it described a format with zero basis in reality.

tdd_steps.expected_failure: cargo test -p lumen-session --test test_codex fails to compile against the current codex.rs/fingerprint.rs (choices[]/thread_id-at-top-level/summed-usage logic): session_id assertion fails ("codex-session" != "thread-abc123"), turns.len() assertion fails (0 != 3), and `service_tier` fails to compile until TASK-SESSION-000 has landed.
tdd_steps.implementation: In crates/lumen-session/src/fingerprint.rs, replace the Codex branch with: `if sample_str.contains("\"type\":\"event_msg\"") || sample_str.contains("\"type\":\"response_item\"") { return Some(OrchestratorKind::Codex); }`. Rewrite crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/codex.rs's matches_fingerprint to `sample.contains("\"type\":\"event_msg\"") || sample.contains("\"type\":\"response_item\"")` (CRIT-LUMEN-108 parity with detect_orchestrator). Rewrite parse_stream to: iterate lines; on JSON parse failure push a ParseFailureRecord and continue; skip any line where `val.get("type").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) != Some("event_msg")`; branch on `payload.get("type").and_then(|v| v.as_str())`: for "item_completed", set session_id from `payload.get("thread_id")`, map `payload.item.type` to TurnRole via {"UserMessage"=>User, "AgentMessage"=>Assistant, "CommandExecution"|"Reasoning"=>ToolResult, _=>System}, set text from `payload.item.text`, push a CanonicalTurn; for "token_count", if `payload.total_token_usage` is present overwrite (not add to) input_tokens/output_tokens/reasoning_output_tokens from its fields, else leave them at their last value; for "thread_settings_applied", set `service_tier = payload.thread_settings.service_tier.map(CompactString::new)`. After the loop, build `let mut economics = TokenEconomics::calculate(input_tokens, output_tokens, 0, 0, &model_family); economics.reasoning_output_tokens = reasoning_output_tokens;` and include `service_tier,` and `parse_failures,` in the final CanonicalTranscript literal.
tdd_steps.expected_pass: cargo test -p lumen-session --test test_codex passes: fingerprint-under-1ms, turn-role-mapping, cumulative-not-summed-token-accounting, and service_tier assertions all pass.

tasks.title: OpenCodeAdapter Real SQLite Backing: Magic-Header Fingerprint, Fingerprint Parity & Message-Table Token/Cost Summation
tasks.reasoning: Full rewrite. The prior CRIT-LUMEN-107/108 fingerprinted and parsed an invented action/observation/source JSONL shape confirmed this session, via CodeBurn's own source comment plus direct sqlite3 inspection of a real local ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db, to match no real OpenCode version ever. Current OpenCode is SQLite-backed (session/message/part/event tables), so fingerprinting keys on the 16-byte SQLite file magic header, and real parsing requires random-access file I/O incompatible with the SessionAdapter::parse_stream(Box<dyn BufRead>) trait method. Decision (explicit, not deferred): OpenCodeAdapter keeps matches_fingerprint/capabilities/parse_stream to satisfy the SessionAdapter trait (parse_stream becomes a thin byte-sniffing entry point that returns IngestionError::UnrecognizedFormat for non-SQLite input, since a BufRead-oriented caller cannot feed it a real .db file), and gains a new inherent method `parse_sqlite_session(&self, db_path: &Path) -> Result<CanonicalTranscript, IngestionError>` that opens the file directly with rusqlite and sums message table's confirmed-real precomputed columns (tokens_input, tokens_output, tokens_reasoning, tokens_cache_read, tokens_cache_write, cost) per CRIT-LUMEN-111. CRIT-LUMEN-112/113/114 (part-table role/text/tool-call columns, legacy file-based generation, event-table error columns) are covered separately by TASK-SESSION-010 as explicit open items, per the spec's own reasoning that no real sample was inspected closely enough this session to name those columns without fabricating them.

tdd_steps.failing_test: Add `rusqlite = { workspace = true }` to crates/lumen-session/Cargo.toml's [dependencies]. Add to crates/lumen-fixtures/src/db.rs: `pub struct OpenCodeTestDb { pub dir: TempDir, pub db_path: Utf8PathBuf } pub fn create_opencode_test_db() -> OpenCodeTestDb { let dir = tempdir().expect("tempdir"); let db_path = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(dir.path().join("opencode.db")).unwrap(); let conn = rusqlite::Connection::open(&db_path).expect("open sqlite"); conn.execute_batch("CREATE TABLE session (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY); CREATE TABLE message (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, session_id TEXT, cost REAL, tokens_input INTEGER, tokens_output INTEGER, tokens_reasoning INTEGER, tokens_cache_read INTEGER, tokens_cache_write INTEGER); INSERT INTO session (id) VALUES ('sess-1'); INSERT INTO message (id, session_id, cost, tokens_input, tokens_output, tokens_reasoning, tokens_cache_read, tokens_cache_write) VALUES ('m1','sess-1',0.05,1200,80,10,900,0), ('m2','sess-1',0.03,600,40,5,300,0);").expect("seed"); drop(conn); OpenCodeTestDb { dir, db_path } } -- deliberately a NEW, lighter struct (not the existing TestDatabaseDouble/SqliteStore double): this test only ever calls adapter.parse_sqlite_session(db.db_path), which opens its own independent rusqlite::Connection on that path -- a lumen-store SqliteStore handle is never read by anything in this test, and reopening one would silently run lumen-store's full migration suite against the temp file as an unstated side effect (audit finding, 2026-08-21: the prior 'for consistency' framing named no real consistency requirement, since nothing else in the test needs a lumen-store handle).` -- rewrite test_opencode.rs to replace the JSONL-based test entirely with: a fingerprint test asserting `detect_orchestrator(b"SQLite format 3\0...")` returns Some(OrchestratorKind::OpenCode) in under 1ms (CRIT-LUMEN-107); a parity test asserting `OpenCodeAdapter.matches_fingerprint` agrees with `detect_orchestrator` on both a real SQLite-header sample and a non-matching sample (CRIT-LUMEN-108); and `#[test] fn test_opencode_adapter_sums_message_table_tokens_and_cost() { let db = lumen_fixtures::create_opencode_test_db(); let adapter = OpenCodeAdapter; let transcript = adapter.parse_sqlite_session(db.db_path.as_std_path()).expect("parse"); assert_eq!(transcript.economics.input_tokens, 1800); assert_eq!(transcript.economics.output_tokens, 120); assert_eq!(transcript.economics.reasoning_output_tokens, 15); assert_eq!(transcript.economics.cache_read_tokens, 1200); assert!((transcript.economics.total_cost_usd - 0.08).abs() < 0.001); }` (CRIT-LUMEN-111) plus a malformed-row test seeding one row with a NULL in a NOT-expected-nullable column and asserting it lands in `transcript.parse_failures` rather than panicking (CRIT-LUMEN-115).
tdd_steps.expected_failure: cargo test -p lumen-session --test test_opencode fails to compile: `error[E0599]: no method named 'parse_sqlite_session' found for struct 'OpenCodeAdapter'`, and detect_orchestrator/matches_fingerprint still match on the old action/observation substrings, not the SQLite magic header.
tdd_steps.implementation: In crates/lumen-session/src/fingerprint.rs, replace the OpenCode branch with: `if sample_bytes.starts_with(b"SQLite format 3\0") { return Some(OrchestratorKind::OpenCode); }` (must run only after the ClaudeCode/Antigravity/Codex checks, matching current ordering). In crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/opencode.rs: rewrite matches_fingerprint to `sample.as_bytes().starts_with(b"SQLite format 3\0")`; change parse_stream's body to `Err(IngestionError::UnrecognizedFormat)` (BufRead cannot carry a real SQLite file; this method is retained only to satisfy the SessionAdapter trait) with a doc comment explaining why, per this task's reasoning; add a new `impl OpenCodeAdapter` block containing `pub fn parse_sqlite_session(&self, db_path: &std::path::Path) -> Result<CanonicalTranscript, IngestionError>` that opens the db with `rusqlite::Connection::open`, runs `SELECT cost, tokens_input, tokens_output, tokens_reasoning, tokens_cache_read, tokens_cache_write FROM message`, accumulates the six sums via `row.get::<_, Option<i64>>`/`Option<f64>` with `.unwrap_or(0)`/`.unwrap_or(0.0)` per row, records a ParseFailureRecord (session_id: "opencode-session".into(), line_number: row index, byte_offset: 0, error: row error text) for any row that fails to deserialize instead of propagating the error, and builds `let mut economics = TokenEconomics::calculate(input_tokens, output_tokens, 0, cache_read_tokens, &model_family); economics.reasoning_output_tokens = reasoning_tokens; economics.total_cost_usd = total_cost;` before constructing the final CanonicalTranscript with `orchestrator: OrchestratorKind::OpenCode, service_tier: None, otel_conversation_id: None, parse_failures,`.
tdd_steps.expected_pass: cargo test -p lumen-session --test test_opencode passes: SQLite-magic-header fingerprint, matches_fingerprint/detect_orchestrator parity, message-table token/cost summation, and malformed-row-resilience tests all pass.

tasks.title: ClaudeCodeAdapter Subagent Linking, Explicit-Null Rejection & OTel Conversation ID Precedence
tasks.reasoning: New task. CRIT-LUMEN-026 was previously (incorrectly) attached to TASK-SESSION-002 (the AGY task) even though it is entirely about ClaudeCodeAdapter's is_sidechain field and sibling subagents/<worker>.jsonl files; moved here. Two sub-behaviors, both explicit design decisions since the spec leaves the mechanism open: (1) within a single parse_stream call, entries with is_sidechain=true are excluded from the main transcript's turns (they belong to a subagent branch, not the main chain) -- testable via parse_stream alone, no filesystem needed. (2) sibling-file discovery and linking (parent_session_id + subagent_role) requires knowing the session directory, which parse_stream's Box<dyn BufRead> signature does not carry -- implemented as a new inherent method `parse_session_with_subagents(&self, session_dir: &Path, main_file_name: &str) -> Result<CanonicalTranscript, IngestionError>` that reads the main file plus any `session_dir/subagents/*.jsonl` files it finds, unconditionally linking each found file as a child transcript (the spec's orphan-file/orphan-entry non-error clause is satisfied by this being unconditional: a subagents file with no is_sidechain entries referencing it back in the main file is still linked without error, per the criterion's literal 'not an error' framing). CRIT-LUMEN-163 and CRIT-LUMEN-164 are new, purely within parse_stream, and colocated here because both are ClaudeCodeAdapter-specific corrections to the same file this task otherwise touches.

tdd_steps.failing_test: Add four tests to test_claude.rs: (1) `test_claude_code_adapter_excludes_sidechain_entries_from_main_turns`: a sample with one `is_sidechain:true` user entry and one normal entry; assert `transcript.turns.len() == 1` and the surviving turn is the non-sidechain one. (2) `test_claude_code_adapter_links_subagent_transcript_file`: using `tempfile::tempdir()`, write `main.jsonl` (one normal entry with sessionId "parent-1") and `subagents/worker-a.jsonl` (one entry) into the temp dir; call `ClaudeCodeAdapter.parse_session_with_subagents(dir.path(), "main.jsonl")`; assert `transcript.subagents.len() == 1`, `transcript.subagents[0].parent_session_id == Some("parent-1".into())`, `transcript.subagents[0].subagent_role == Some("worker-a".into())`. (3) `test_claude_code_adapter_rejects_explicit_null_session_id`: a sample line `{"type":"user","sessionId":null,"message":{"role":"user","content":"hi"}}`; assert the resulting transcript has `parse_failures.len() == 1` and `turns.len() == 0`. (4) `test_claude_code_adapter_otel_conversation_id_first_non_sidechain_wins`: three entries -- a sidechain entry with requestId "req-side", then a non-sidechain entry with requestId "req-first", then a second non-sidechain entry with requestId "req-second"; assert `transcript.otel_conversation_id == Some("req-first".into())`.
tdd_steps.expected_failure: cargo test -p lumen-session --test test_claude fails: test (1) fails because is_sidechain is not currently read at all (turns.len() == 2, not 1); test (2) fails to compile with `error[E0599]: no method named 'parse_session_with_subagents' found`; test (3) fails because `sessionId: null` is currently read via `.and_then(|v| v.as_str())`, which silently treats null the same as absent, so no parse_failures entry is recorded; test (4) fails because otel_conversation_id is never set (stays None).
tdd_steps.implementation: In claude.rs's parse_stream: after parsing `val`, add a null-field guard before any other field extraction: `for field in ["id", "cwd", "model", "sessionId", "requestId", "version", "costUSD", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens"] { if val.get(field).map(|v| v.is_null()).unwrap_or(false) { parse_failures.push(ParseFailureRecord { session_id: session_id.clone(), line_number: idx + 1, byte_offset: 0, error: CompactString::new(format!("explicit null on field '{field}'")) }); continue 'lines; } }` (wrap the existing per-line loop body in a labeled `'lines: for (idx, line_res) in ...` so `continue 'lines` skips the rest of this line's processing -- CRIT-LUMEN-163). Add `let is_sidechain = val.get("is_sidechain").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false); if is_sidechain { continue; }` immediately after the null-field guard, before any turn-pushing logic (CRIT-LUMEN-026 part 1). Add `let mut otel_conversation_id: Option<CompactString> = None; ... if otel_conversation_id.is_none() && !is_sidechain { if let Some(rid) = val.get("requestId").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) { otel_conversation_id = Some(CompactString::new(rid)); } }` inside the loop, and include `otel_conversation_id,` in the final CanonicalTranscript literal (CRIT-LUMEN-164). Add a new `impl ClaudeCodeAdapter` block: `pub fn parse_session_with_subagents(&self, session_dir: &std::path::Path, main_file_name: &str) -> Result<CanonicalTranscript, IngestionError> { let main_path = session_dir.join(main_file_name); let main_file = std::fs::File::open(&main_path)?; let mut transcript = self.parse_stream(Box::new(std::io::BufReader::new(main_file)))?; let subagents_dir = session_dir.join("subagents"); if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&subagents_dir) { for entry in entries.flatten() { let path = entry.path(); if path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) != Some("jsonl") { continue; } let worker = path.file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("unknown").to_string(); let file = std::fs::File::open(&path)?; let mut child = self.parse_stream(Box::new(std::io::BufReader::new(file)))?; child.parent_session_id = Some(transcript.session_id.clone()); child.subagent_role = Some(CompactString::new(worker)); transcript.subagents.push(child); } } Ok(transcript) }` (CRIT-LUMEN-026 part 2).
tdd_steps.expected_pass: cargo test -p lumen-session --test test_claude passes: all 4 new tests plus the existing TASK-SESSION-001 tests in the same file pass cleanly.

tasks.title: OpenCode Part-Table Schema Discovery Spike (CRIT-LUMEN-112/113/114 Open Items)
tasks.reasoning: These three criteria are explicitly marked judgment_call:true open items in the spec itself -- the spec's own reasoning states the part table's role/text/tool-call column layout, the legacy file-based generation's shape, and the event table's error columns were NOT closely enough inspected this session to name literal fields without fabricating them (see non_goals: 'a follow-up pass with real sample data is required before those criteria's literal field names can be finalized'). Per the amendment instructions, this task does not guess column names. Instead it is a concrete, mechanically-executable spike: run a real schema-introspection command against a live opencode.db and record the exact output. THE DONE CONDITION is either (a) real column names are discovered and hardcoded, turning the test green, or (b) no real opencode.db is available to the implementer, in which case the exact, unambiguous outcome is to leave the test marked #[ignore] with the reason string below and commit that state -- this is not a design decision left to the implementer; the spec's non_goals section already made this decision.

tdd_steps.implementation: Create crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/opencode_schema.rs with: `/// CRIT-LUMEN-112: returns the real part-table column names for role/text/tool-call discrimination once confirmed via `sqlite3 <path> 'PRAGMA table_info(part);'` against a real, installed OpenCode instance.
